meta.purpose: Static venue/park reference table keyed on franchise_id, for downstream park-factor work.
meta.note: Unlike artifacts/latest/**, this file is NOT a pure function of games/**. It is hand-researched from external sources (mostly Wikipedia and Pioneer League / local-news coverage, fetched via WebSearch/WebFetch on 2026-08-31) because meta.source_url in every game file 403s from this container (CloudFront block) and the raw scraped HTML is deliberately not committed (see README, caller contract clause 3). It therefore does NOT carry a `generated_at` in the sense scripts/check_artifacts_current.py checks for, and is intentionally kept outside artifacts/latest/ so that script's fixed (module, builder) list never has to know about it. See scripts/build_venues.py for the one thing that IS mechanically checked: that every franchise_id appearing in games/** has an entry here, and that `seasons_in_corpus` matches the corpus.

confidence_values.verified: a specific claim (park name/address/coords/elevation/orientation) was read directly off a source fetched during this research pass
confidence_values.probable: inferred rather than read directly -- most commonly a CITY elevation used as a stand-in for the park's (unsurveyed) elevation, or a park identity carried over from adjacent, consistent reporting rather than a single authoritative page
confidence_values.unknown: not established; field is null rather than guessed

meta.orientation_caveat: Ballpark 'orientation' sources almost universally describe alignment as a coarse compass label (e.g. 'aligned northeast, home plate to second base'), not a surveyed azimuth. field_orientation_deg_approx maps that label onto the nearest 32-point compass heading (NE=45, SE=135, ...; 'north by east' = 11.25) and is explicitly an approximation of an approximation -- do not treat it as a precise home-to-center-field azimuth. Home-to-second-base is used as a proxy for home-to-center-field, which is the standard ballpark-alignment convention in these sources (the two lines coincide by construction of the diamond).
meta.neutral_site_and_relocation_finding: A static franchise_id -> venue table CANNOT see a neutral-site game, and this research surfaced at least one concrete case where a naive corpus-wide mapping would be wrong: the real-world club behind franchise:4e7dd733f635c973 (corpus name 'Yuba-Sutter Freebirds' in ALL of 2024/2025/2026) played its actual 2024 season as the 'Yolo High Wheelers' at Phil Swimley Field / Dobbins Stadium in Davis, CA, then relocated to Bryant Field in Marysville, CA starting in 2025, and only took the 'Freebirds' name in Feb 2026. That is a real venue change mid-corpus that a single venues.json franchises.<id>.home_park field would hide -- which is why this file gives 'venues' as a LIST of {years, park...} entries per franchise rather than one park per franchise. No other evidence of a neutral-site or mid-corpus relocated game was found for the other 14 franchises in 2024-2026 -- but that is an absence-of-evidence finding (general news searches, not a play-by-play audit), not a guarantee. See the accompanying report for the full discussion.
meta.redpocket_mobiles_finding: franchise:5252121b77b845ba (RedPocket Mobiles) plays 0 of 83 2026 games at a home park BY DESIGN, not because of a delayed stadium: it is a deliberate barnstorming/travelling club (sponsor-named, all-road-games concept) confirmed by the Pioneer League's own announcement and independent coverage. Represented here as travelling: true, home_park: null rather than as missing data.
meta.keyed_by: franchise_id -> season -> venue. One explicit row per (franchise, season) actually present in games/**. Venues are NOT expressed as year ranges: independent-league clubs change stadia more often than a range implies, so continuity is never inferred silently -- each season states its own park and says, via park_season_link, whether that link was researched for that specific year.

park_season_link_values.evidenced: the park<->season link was researched for THIS specific season (the club's year-by-year venue history was checked, not assumed).
park_season_link_values.assumed: the park was established for the club generally, then carried to this season without year-specific verification. NOT a claim that the club is known to have played there that year. Downgrade to a researched value before relying on it for a season-specific park factor.

meta.data_cross_check: The corpus itself can corroborate or contradict a claimed relocation, because a park change should move the run environment. One check was run: franchise:4e7dd733f635c973 (Yuba-Sutter Freebirds) is recorded here as Dobbins Stadium (Davis) in 2024 and Bryant Field (Marysville) from 2025. The play-by-play does NOT support that boundary -- 2024 and 2025 are nearly identical (11.9 R/G in both; within-player park index 0.912 vs 0.859), while the franchise's large environment shift is 2025->2026 (index 0.859 -> 1.032, 11.9 -> 18.8 R/G). Either the two parks play alike, or the relocation year is wrong. Treat these two rows as unresolved.

Real 2026 Pioneer League club, deliberately built as a sponsor-named barnstorming/travelling team with NO home ballpark -- all 96 scheduled games (83 of which are in this corpus, all recorded as 'away') are on the road, by design, not due to a delayed or unready stadium. Confirmed by the league's own announcement and independent coverage (Yahoo Finance headline: 'A Team With No Home: RedPocket Mobiles To Launch All-Access Baseball Docuseries'; quote from team lead Dmitri Young: 'We're a barnstorming team... going back to the grass roots of what baseball is'). No home city/base is reported anywhere found. This matches the corpus exactly: 0 of 83 2026 games are home games for this franchise_id.  OPEN QUESTION (repo owner, 2026-08-31): the club may simply be a TEMPORARY placeholder holding a schedule slot until a permanent expansion franchise takes it -- the punning sponsor name ('Mobiles' = mobile/no fixed home) reads as deliberate on that theory. That is compatible with the sourced 'barnstorming by design' framing and with the corpus (0 home games in 83), but it changes the downstream reading: a placeholder that disappears after 2026 should not be carried forward as a standing franchise. Unresolved -- do not encode either reading as fact.
